name: bubble-tri
comment: TRIANGULAR BUBBLE TILES (Chase, Field & McCluer, 'Puzzle Pieces and Bubble Tiles', working draft 2026-08-22). A bubble tile is an equilateral polygon whose every edge carries one of two states, a BUMP that protrudes or a BITE that is cut in, with a COMPLEMENTARY matching rule: a bump must meet a bite, and two bumps or two bites cannot meet. The four triangular tiles are the four binary necklaces of length 3 (OEIS A000031), the paper's T0/T1/T2/T3, named here by bite count. B = bump, I = bIte, both at unit length: the arcs are a decoration and the developed substrate is the plain triangular tiling. Angles in D=24 units: 60 = 4, six to a vertex, so maxValence 6 is exact and not a bound. "edgeComplement" flips gen_alphabet's vertex-adjacency predicate; the SEARCH needs EU_EDGE_COMPL=1 and the developer --complement, and develop_marked re-checks every glue so a run that forgets the knob fails loudly instead of emitting a wrong catalogue. Reflections: all four tiles are achiral (each necklace's reverse is one of its own rotations), so no mirror twins appear and the k counts here are directly comparable to the merge-mirrors convention the rest of the atlas uses.
